title: I'm a bit worried after posting this. What is your opinion of the whole thing, does anyone already have experience with a game they have published where they used AI art? It looks like the safe way at the moment is not to say that you have used AI Art in your game. Looking at Steam,...etc.
author: 0nlynOmadsaref3

comments.author: Beginning-Chapter-26
comments.body: [I'll just put my game up on the Epic Games store if Steam still rejects games with AI.](https://twitter.com/TimSweeneyEpic/status/1698028441994506322?t=CB35gnCZ6VIzILupEnpphw&s=19)

replies.author: 0nlynOmadsaref3
replies.body:
haha, yes, I saw that post too. 

I'll probably do that too, or on Steam just not say anything and in Epic Games Store mark it as AI Art Game but maybe rather not say anything anywhere. 

But I think there will be changes in the platforms' policies. 

Epic Games can't just say we're going to allow this anyway, no matter what the law, the courts, say.

replies.author: Samanjaa
replies.body: Sadly, adult content game cannot release as *self*\-publishing on EGS. Only if your game directly approve by Epic Games or being a AAA company in the case of Cyberpunk 2077.

replies.author: Beginning-Chapter-26
replies.body: This is news to me. What would be considered "adult" to Epic?

comments.author: IgnisIncendio
comments.body: Just use more friendly stores like Epic or Itch. Wait for the dust to settle first in regards to Steam; the climate of opinion will surely change in time. I would like to add on that U.S. copyright law is obviously not the only copyright law that matters, so a lot of the answers in the original question don't make sense from an international standpoint. In particular, Singapore specifically allows AI training, so that copyright is likely not an issue. EU too, I believe. Check out Text and Data Mining Exemptions.

replies.author: 0nlynOmadsaref3
replies.body:
Thank you for your answer, it helped to calm my nerves a bit. 

I will definitely read the article, thanks for the link. 

Yes, sitting it out is the only thing we can do now....

Itch and Epic are definitely my first go-to points once the game is finished. 

Let's see how the rules develop there.

comments.author: Laicbeias
comments.body: steams lawyers are just "yo if there is a ruling that all AI generated artworks are considered copyright infringement guess who will get sued? the distributor. lets not do this"

replies.author: 0nlynOmadsaref3
replies.body:
I totally understand, and I'm not mad at Steam at all. 

From a business point of view, it makes perfect sense.

comments.author: Raradev01
comments.body:
It's interesting how this whole discussion seems to revolve around Steam.  I've seen a ton of apps that openly use ChatGPT on Google Play, for example, including the official ChatGPT app.  The Apple Store also has the official ChatGPT app.  There's also a bunch of AI art apps on both platforms.

It would appear as if neither Apple nor Google really see this situation in the terrifying way that Valve does.

In some ways that's not surprising -- tech giants likely intend to use this technology themselves all over the place, so why try to keep it off their app stores?

I almost think we'll be most likely to see generative AI used in mobile games well before it catches on in the PC market, almost entirely because of Valve's stance.  I suppose reasonable people can disagree on whether that's a good thing or a bad thing...
